limitations: This full-width screen uses fixed p128/d8 fresh-server widths; it does not cover dynamic arrivals, overload, soak, long context, graph changes, COW, or eviction.
Large block spread at selected widths and the c32 reversal versus the core screen show that a single width or order block cannot justify a queue default.
Runtime queue IDs/count remain unobserved until cache-only rocprof; configured/effective environment is recorded and unset removes GPU_MAX_HW_QUEUES.
Production cross-admission generated-ID equality is diagnostic; exact control repeatability and the external same-schedule numerical gate are binding.

findings: No queue policy wins generically across widths; queue2 has the highest 13-width geometric-mean throughput, with queue1/4/8/unset lower by 0.75/0.64/0.50/0.42%.
The core-screen queue8 c32 advantage does not reproduce: full-width queue8 loses to queue2 in both c32 blocks (-3.68%/-6.90%, paired median -5.29%).
Queue8 wins c1/c2/c4 rollups, but c2 and c4 have 10-15% block spread; they cannot select a policy.
All policies pass all six measured SLO runs through c7; c8 is partial (1-3/6), and c9+ has zero SLO-passing runs.
Truly unset is mechanically stable but offers no generic performance advantage; its aggregate geometric mean is 0.42% below queue2.
verdict.next: Keep queue2 as the current control without a new promotion. Run arrival/pressure/soak and context/graph/COW/eviction matrices for all five policies before adjudication.
